Spearman rank correlations (rho), one observation per MM over the 148 wallets.

  • Deviation MAD mostly tracks position size.
    Its rank correlation with median |position| is 0.94. So a move measured in MADs asks whether it is large for that MM, not whether it is large in HYPE.
  • Short-horizon inventory volatility is different.
    Its correlation with median |position| is only 0.64, and volatility as a share of median |position| falls sharply as that position grows (rho −0.89). MMs with small positions turn over a larger fraction of them.

5.4 Shock rate and minutes to half

  • Minutes to half: minutes after t1 until half of the MM's position change over the event is back, capped at 360 (360 = not within 6 hours).
Terms used here: sig24, Shocked, Absorber, absorption share, Control window, Markout M30, M60, M120, Submits, cancels, Minutes to half, Censored, One-sided, two-sided, rho, Quantile cells
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Absorber, absorption share: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event. Absorption rank orders them by that maker USD, 1 = largest.
  • Control window: for each event, the same UTC clock time and length on the nearest date (+1, −1, +2, −2, … days) with no event in the window or within 2 hours of it. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.
  • Markout M30, M60, M120: what a fill is worth against the mid 30, 60 or 120 minutes later, in bps of the fill's USD; positive is favourable to the wallet.
  • Submits, cancels: new limit orders and cancels. The venue records a modify as one cancel plus one new order, so cancels per submit sits near 1.
  • Minutes to half: minutes after t1 until half of the MM's position change over the event is back, capped at 360 (360 = not within 6 hours).
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
  • One-sided, two-sided: an event is one-sided when the hit side's taker USD surges and the other side's does not; two-sided when both surge.
  • rho: Spearman rank correlation, from −1 to +1; p tests rho = 0.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.

Spearman's rank correlation ρ and its test

  • ρ ranks the wallets separately on the state variable and on the outcome, then takes the ordinary correlation of the two rank lists. With no ties, ρ = 1−6∑idi2n(n2−1), where di is wallet i's rank on one variable minus its rank on the other and n is the number of wallets.
  • Reading it. ρ runs from −1 to +1. +1 means the outcome always rises with the state variable, −1 means it always falls, and 0 means the two orderings are unrelated. It measures any monotone relation, not only a straight line, and a single very large wallet cannot drive it because only ranks enter.
  • The test. p is the two-sided p-value for the null hypothesis ρ = 0: the probability of a |ρ| at least this large if the two variables were independent across wallets. It treats wallets as independent observations.

Spearman tests across wallets, one observation per wallet, not per event; every date, 2025-10-10 included, on the §4.1 active-MM rule. n counts wallets: for the pre-event rows, the 881 wallets with at least 20 active event windows; for the lifetime rows, the 148 wallets of the §5.1 profile among them; for the rows on median minutes to half, those with at least five shocks as well (254 wallets, 108 with a profile). Shock rate is the share of that wallet’s own active event windows in which it was shocked, so it is a per-wallet frequency between 0 and 1. Median minutes to half is the median over that wallet’s own shocks, and is capped at 360 minutes (censored). State variables come in two families: pre-event ones are that wallet’s median across its event windows, lifetime ones are the §5.1 profile variables computed over all its active bins. rho is Spearman; p is its two-sided p-value, printed as <1e−4 below that value. Source tables/pop_orderfixact_alldates/redef2_pop_population_test.csv.

Large MMs are shocked more often; active MMs recover faster. Position size predicts shock rate (rho +0.53 to +0.72 for median |position| before events and over the lifetime, lifetime deviation MAD and lifetime inventory volatility), while lifetime trades and submits per bin do not (+0.08 and +0.07, p = 0.310 and 0.422). For minutes to half the two swap places: activity predicts a fast return (absorption share −0.64, trades per bin −0.36, submits per bin −0.32), and lifetime median |position| predicts a slow one (+0.63). Lifetime inventory volatility changes sign between the two outcomes. The wallets shocked most often get back to half fastest (−0.20).

Most of the size result comes from the $12,500 floor in the own position scale, not from behavior. The own scale is the largest of three numbers, and the third is a flat $12,500 of HYPE (§4.1). Where that floor sets the scale, a shock needs a $37,500 position change, which a small MM almost never makes. The floor sets the scale in 66% of the 113,898 active wallet-event rows with a non-zero pre-event position (every date; sig24 in dollars at the window-start mid within 1% of $12,500). Where the scale comes from the wallet’s own history, the size relation does not survive: rho is +0.45 on the 577 wallets whose floor binds in over 80% of their windows, and −0.14 (p = 0.22) on the 79 wallets where it binds in under 20%. The size result is mostly this floor. The activity result does not depend on it.
Two limits on every row. The four scale variables are close to one variable: lifetime deviation MAD against lifetime median |position| is rho +0.94 on the 148 profile wallets. And the speed outcome is heavily censored: median minutes to half is capped at 360 minutes (§4.4). Over the 254 wallets with at least five shocks its p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95 are 9 / 88 / 238 / 360 / 360, so at least a quarter sit at the cap and the top of the ranking is ties. Every rho is bivariate, with no controls.
Population and measurement caveats

The active-day rule deliberately removes sporadic wallets, so these 148 MMs are an active cohort rather than every address ever labelled MM. Position levels use the exchange-reported fill chain; the drifting hype_mm_5m.inventory_open_size level is not used. Correlations are descriptive and do not identify strategy or skill.

8. Biggest absorbers against flagged MMs

Event set 1: 914 of the 915 net-flow events on 30-minute boxes, every date included, with 126,846 event × wallet rows. The end rule reads the position at t1; the peak rule reads it at every minute from t0 to t1.
  • End rule, peak rule: the end rule flags |position at t1 − position at t0| ≥ 3 sig24; the peak rule applies the same test to the largest gap from the t0 position at any minute inside the window.
Terms used here: Event window, sig24, Shocked, End rule, peak rule, Absorber, absorption share
  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • End rule, peak rule: the end rule flags |position at t1 − position at t0| ≥ 3 sig24; the peak rule applies the same test to the largest gap from the t0 position at any minute inside the window.
  • Absorber, absorption share: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event. Absorption rank orders them by that maker USD, 1 = largest.

The five wallets that fill most of the surging taker flow are usually not the wallets the end rule flags. It flags none of them in 38.4% of events (351 of 914, fill-based active-MM gate, every date) and one or none in two events out of three. The reason is the wallet's own scale: the absorbers make the largest inventory moves in the event and carry the largest sig24, so the same move, measured from the median position of the 2 hours before, is a median 2.2 in sig24 units, below the threshold of 3.

Population and grain
  • Population. The 914 catalogue events with population measurements, and every active MM of each event (a fill in the 2 hours before and a fill inside the window). 126,846 event × wallet rows. Every table below uses every date, 2025-10-10 included: 126,846 rows and 914 events with five ranked absorbers.
  • Grain. One row is one wallet in one event. Quantiles are unweighted across rows.

8.1 Definitions

Terms and the two rules
  • Hit side. The taker side that surged: taker sells in a net-sell event, taker buys in a net-buy event.
  • Absorption and rank. A wallet's maker volume on the side that fills those takers, summed over the 30-minute window. absorb_rank orders the event's active MMs by it; the top-5 absorbers are ranks 1 to 5.
  • Position path. q(t) is the exchange-reported HYPE position at the end of the 1-minute bin, rebuilt from grouped_trade_oid. A 1-minute bin is labeled by its start, so the level at clock time t is the bin labeled t−1 minute. t0 is the window start, t1 the window end.
  • Own scale. sig24 is the wallet's own 24-hour robust inventory scale, defined in §4.1. Both rules below use the same threshold of 3.

Two rules are compared throughout this section. They differ in one place: which minute of the window the position is read at.

  • End rule, the shock rule of record (§4.1): flag the wallet when |q(t1)−q(t0)|≥3×sig24
  • Peak rule: flag the wallet when the position gets that far from the same start level at any minute of the window, maxt0≤t≤t1|q(t)−q(t0)|≥3×sig24
  • Peak excursion E is the left side of the peak rule, reported in HYPE, in USD at the mid of the peak minute, and divided by sig24. A variant measures it from the median position of the 2 hours before the window, b=median2h(q), instead of from q(t0); 8.5 shows why the rule comparison does not carry that baseline. Tables 44 and 45 and the 2.2 sig24 median use it.
  • Retained fraction |q(t1)−b|/maxt|q(t)−b|. 1 means the position was at its furthest when the window closed; 0.3 means 70% of the largest move was already given back.

  • zdq: the position change from t0 to t1 divided by the MM's own sig24.

  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • zdq: the position change from t0 to t1 divided by the MM's own sig24.
  • End rule, peak rule: the end rule flags |position at t1 − position at t0| ≥ 3 sig24; the peak rule applies the same test to the largest gap from the t0 position at any minute inside the window.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • Absorber, absorption share: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event. Absorption rank orders them by that maker USD, 1 = largest.
  • Quantile cells: a cell with five numbers is p5 / p25 / p50 / p75 / p95; with three, p25 / p50 / p75.

8.4 How much of the peak is held at the end

  • Wallet codes: T01 to T10 are the largest takers of a replay, X## the largest non-roster makers, V01 the largest liquidated wallet.
Terms used here: Event window, Active MM, sig24, Shocked, End rule, peak rule, Absorber, absorption share, Taker share, Roster, Wallet codes
  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it.
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • End rule, peak rule: the end rule flags |position at t1 − position at t0| ≥ 3 sig24; the peak rule applies the same test to the largest gap from the t0 position at any minute inside the window.
  • Absorber, absorption share: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event. Absorption rank orders them by that maker USD, 1 = largest.
  • Taker share: the share of a wallet's fill USD in which its own order crossed the spread.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • Wallet codes: T01 to T10 are the largest takers of a replay, X## the largest non-roster makers, V01 the largest liquidated wallet. Codes are local to a section: the same code can name another wallet elsewhere.

All three rules use the threshold 3×sig24 and differ only in which position is compared with which baseline: the end rule takes the position at the window end against q(t0); the start-baseline peak rule takes the furthest q(t) against q(t0); the pre-2h peak rule takes the furthest q(t) against the median position of the 2 hours before the window.   • The peak rule adds 20 points to the top-5 flagged share, 17 points to absorb ranks 6 to 20 and 1.5 points to the other active MMs.
    Events with none of the five flagged fall from 38.4% to 14.7%, and events with three or more rise from 17% to 40%. Every row the end rule flags is flagged by the start-baseline peak rule except 4 rows, 1 of them a top-5 absorber, where the stored and recomputed positions differ slightly at the threshold.
  • The pre-2h baseline mixes pre-window drift into the event, so the start level is the baseline to carry.
    Of the 4,822 rows of other active MMs that the pre-2h peak rule flags and the end rule does not, 48% had already moved twice their own scale or more from their pre-2h median before the window opened, and only 27% are flagged from the start level. It also drops 783 end-flagged rows, 100 of them top-5 absorbers, whose end level is nearer the pre-2h median than their start level was.
  • A peak rule would name a flagged population 65% larger, concentrated in each event's top 20 absorbers.
    No result in §4 uses the peak rule; adopting it means rerunning §4 and the results built on it.
Measurement caveats

The end-minus-start change recomputed from the rebuilt 1-minute positions equals the stored dq_hype within 0.01 HYPE on 99.08% of rows. The 1,165 rows that differ do so by a median 38 HYPE, a median 0.05 of the wallet's own scale, because the two position rebuilds read the fills over different ranges. The shocked flag would change on 7 of 126,846 rows. Every table above uses the stored flag, sig24 and dq_hype. sig24 sits at the $12,500 floor, read at the window-start mid, for 69% of rows, so sigma-scaled percentiles among the small wallets carry ties rather than a ranking. Whether the 26% who reach the threshold and give it back are laying off through their own quotes or hedging in another coin is not tested here; the taker share says the exit is mostly maker fills on HYPE, but the cross-coin book is not checked.

15. Data caveats

  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Bin labels: wallet-shock times are 5-minute bin labels of an end-of-bin position; clock time is the label plus 5 minutes.
  • Surge onset (replays): the first second at which the 30-second sum of hit-side taker USD reaches 3 times the 95th percentile of that sum over the previous 6 hours.
Terms used here: Roster, form_start, peak, Bin labels, Episode, Surge onset (replays)
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Bin labels: wallet-shock times are 5-minute bin labels of an end-of-bin position; clock time is the label plus 5 minutes.
  • Episode: a group of roster shocks that overlap in time.
  • Surge onset (replays): the first second at which the 30-second sum of hit-side taker USD reaches 3 times the 95th percentile of that sum over the previous 6 hours.
  1. Exp8's catalogue times are 5-minute bin labels, and the clock window is the label plus five minutes.
    The 5-minute position is an end-of-bin level, so the bin labelled 02:55 holds the position at clock 03:00, and the flow that builds a shock peaking in bin peak lives in clock [form_start + 5 min, peak + 5 min). Two independent confirmations: the tick engine reproduces Exp8's rollout_flow.hit_usd to the dollar only with the offset (without it the discrepancy is 96.7%), and the liquidation package reproduces forced_usd exactly for all three episode-100 shocks the same way. Exp9 and Exp10 anchor their windows on the labels as clock times, so their PRE window includes the first five minutes of the build and their POST1 window opens five minutes before the true peak. Exp9's main result (a 1.36 bps widening of the same-side quote after the peak) has not yet been re-measured with the offset; that re-run is the first follow-up in the last section.
  2. The 5-minute grid understates fast shocks.
    MM05's 1-minute inventory trough on 2025-12-17 is −133,326 HYPE against the catalogue's −105,696 at the bin end; the amplitude is 90,151 HYPE against 62,606, so the grid is 31% low. Slow shocks that move to a new level and stay are unaffected (MM08: −947,764 against −946,977). If shocks are re-sized, fast shocks that reverse within minutes should be sized on a finer grid.
  3. The running inventory column of the 5-minute MM panel drifts.
    hype_mm_5m.inventory_open_size drifts away from the exchange-reported position (factor 82 for MM02). Re-anchor it daily to the exchange-reported close before reading a level; its changes are fine (§5).
  4. Two candidate rule definitions fail on these data.
    A 3-sigma rule on the standardized imbalance ratio selects nothing because the ratio is bounded and its trailing MAD is about 0.3 (§3). A taker-surge onset defined as 3 times the trailing per-second median fires on the first ordinary trade because 70% of seconds carry no trade (§6).

Also recorded: the market dimension's source_hole flag is False on every HYPE bin, so the two real holes (2025-11-24, 2026-04-23) had to be found by hand; the dense panel's maker_fill_mid_distance_vw_bps is null on every date checked, so quote distances in §4 come from the raw order store.

Synthesis

Who quotes and who carries

Terms used here: Control window
  • Control window: for each event, the same UTC clock time and length on the nearest date (+1, −1, +2, −2, … days) with no event in the window or within 2 hours of it. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.

In the median net-flow event, 115 MMs are filled on the side the takers hit, six of them fill half the absorbed volume, and five end the event carrying an inventory shock. The five were already quoting larger and closer on that side, and control windows show no such lean. Many MMs are filled; few end the event holding the position.

What survives the control windows

Terms used here: Shocked, Control window, One-sided, two-sided
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Control window: for each event, the same UTC clock time and length on the nearest date (+1, −1, +2, −2, … days) with no event in the window or within 2 hours of it. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.
  • One-sided, two-sided: an event is one-sided when the hit side's taker USD surges and the other side's does not; two-sided when both surge.

Where MMs' activity and quote distances after an event match the control windows, the change is ordinary variation, not a strategic reaction, and those nulls stay in the report. Two results survive the controls. The first is the direction of the population's inventory: D, net over gross inventory change across active MMs, is 0.86 at events against 0.54 in control windows. The second is the one-sided skew of a shocked MM's own book afterwards.

Sweep and refill inside one second

Terms used here: Touch
  • Touch: the market's best price on that side: the best bid for a bid, the best ask for an ask.

In the tick replays, the largest single taker orders consume many price levels in one millisecond. The touch is refilled within 30 to 200 ms, with little size. The price settles about a second after the sweep, too fast for any 5-minute or 30-minute measurement to see.

Absorbing versus being flagged

Terms used here: sig24, Shocked, Absorption side, exit side
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.

The five wallets that fill most of the hit-side flow also have the largest inventory swings in normal times. Their largest move in the event is a median 2.2 times their own position scale, under the shock threshold. Flagging on the largest move inside the window (the peak rule) instead of the start-to-end change (the end rule) raises their flagged share from 23.9% to 43.7% and leaves everyone else almost unchanged. The end rule's misses are therefore concentrated in the five largest absorbers. Counted by dollars absorbed, fewer MMs carry an event than §8's shocked counts suggest.

Event trigger and price label

Every event in this report comes from one trigger: 30-minute net taker flow in its top 5%. Whether a move counts as big is a separate decision: against the whole sample, or against its own trailing week. Both big-move flags are carried in the catalogue and the two disagree on 17.8% of events, so neither label overwrites the other.

Limits

Terms used here: HYPE MM
  • HYPE MM: a wallet the project's daily label model (v5d) classes as a HYPE market maker on that date. The label is per date.

Nothing here identifies a causal effect of flow on price, an optimal MM response, or skill. §16 lists the limits in full.

16. Limits

  • SAME, OPP: SAME is the MM side that absorbs the takers (asks when takers buy); OPP is the other side.
Terms used here: Active MM, Shocked, SAME, OPP, Control window, ALO, IOC, GTC, Submits, cancels, Forced, voluntary flow, Roster, Censored, Event classes, One-sided, two-sided
  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • SAME, OPP: SAME is the MM side that absorbs the takers (asks when takers buy); OPP is the other side.
  • Control window: for each event, the same UTC clock time and length on the nearest date (+1, −1, +2, −2, … days) with no event in the window or within 2 hours of it. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.
  • ALO, IOC, GTC: order types: ALO is post-only (rejected if it would cross), IOC is immediate-or-cancel, GTC rests until cancelled.
  • Submits, cancels: new limit orders and cancels. The venue records a modify as one cancel plus one new order, so cancels per submit sits near 1.
  • Forced, voluntary flow: forced flow is taker USD from liquidations and auto-deleveraging (ADL); voluntary flow is all other taker USD. A victim is the wallet that was force-closed.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • Censored: the value hit the cap: the position had not come back by the end of the search window, so the true time is longer.
  • Event classes: liquidation cascade: forced flow at least 10% of taker USD; otherwise big price move: the mid moved at least 168 bps from start to end, the top 5% of all half hours; otherwise no big price move.
  • One-sided, two-sided: an event is one-sided when the hit side's taker USD surges and the other side's does not; two-sided when both surge.
  • Nothing here is causal.
    Flow and price move together inside a bin, and the replays order them in seconds on two events. News, another venue or another coin could drive both, and the HYPE book would not show it. The control windows say what these statistics look like in ordinary half hours, not why an event happened.
  • Two replays are two events.
    The trade-versus-cancel split, the 36-second flow lead, the fresh-quote share and the voluntary lead before the first liquidation are not shown to generalize. The same method can replay more events.
  • The flow cutoff and the price gate are in-sample quantiles.
    The trailing version of the flow cutoff exists and behaves almost identically, 921 events against 915. The 168 bps gate is the full-sample p95; a paper version should say so or use a trailing quantile.
  • One-sided against two-sided depends on the bin size
    (55% at 30 minutes, 91% at 5 minutes) and must always be quoted with it.
  • The control windows are matched on clock time and length only.
    They are not matched on volume or volatility, so an event-minus-control difference mixes "an event happened" with "the market was busy". The direction of that bias is stated where it matters in §4.
  • SAME and OPP are event-relative labels.
    For the few shocked MMs whose position moved with the takers rather than against them (about 5% of shocked wallet-events), "SAME" is still the side that absorbs the market's flow, not the side that built that wallet's position.
  • The order-state measures see limit orders only
    (post-only ALO and ordinary GTC orders, not trigger orders), from placement to the final status row; orders with no final status row are dropped. Modify-in-place is recorded as cancel plus new order by the venue and counts as one cancel and one submit.
  • Equity is the whole account across all coins
    , sampled at snapshot cadence (2 to 5.5 hours), so the change "to the window end" spans more than the event, and a value at exactly +2 h exists for under half of the wallet-events.
  • The 7-day closed-PnL baseline exists only for wallets in the 1,035-wallet dense MM panel
    (91% of active-MM rows; the baseline is realized PnL on position-reducing fills over the previous 7 days); the other 9% have no "worse than usual" flag.
  • Whether a shocked MM was itself liquidated is not answered here.
    Only 1 active MM-event pair is both shocked and liquidated outside 2025-10-10, against 28 on that day, so any split would be a reading of the crash day alone. What the sample does say is that a market cascade is not usually the liquidation of the MMs absorbing it.
  • The population profile has no held-out check
    , and every correlation in §5.4 is bivariate with no controls.
  • Peer medians in the replays are over every MM with a resting quote
    , a heterogeneous set. They show that MM05 and MM08 rest far more size than the other MMs, not that they do so against their own competitor set.
  • Binding-coin attribution uses the last account snapshot
    , a median of 104 minutes old and up to 7 hours for a few large accounts.
  • The liquidation event's forced share is at the 99.94th percentile
    , so it is by construction not a typical cascade; its 361-bps move is a 98th-percentile move.
  • The counterparty test of §4.8 has no matched control.
    It is the one measurement in §4 with no control counterpart, so its 45% has no placebo baseline.

17. Open decisions

17.1 Definitions

  • Wfocus: the shortest interval inside the analysis window that holds 80% of the trough-to-peak mid move.
  • F1, F2, F3: F1: the 922 one-sided side surges.
  • A, L, t*: A is the most HYPE built on the absorption side inside the window, t* the minute it is reached, L the position at t* against the 6-hour median; both are compared with the MM's own sig24.
Terms used here: Event window, Active MM, sig24, Shocked, End rule, peak rule, Absorption side, exit side, Absorber, absorption share, Roster, Wfocus, Surge onset (replays), Peer median, F1, F2, F3, Recall, lift, Event classes, One-sided, two-sided, Effective N, C, D, A, L, t*
  • Event window: the day is cut into 30-minute bins that start at :00 and :30 UTC. A bin is flagged when HYPE net taker flow (taker buys minus taker sells, USD, all wallets) is far from normal: its distance from the median of the previous 7 days of bins, divided by a robust spread of those bins (1.4826 times their median absolute deviation, at least $25,000), is at least 3.70 in absolute value, the cutoff that keeps the top 5% of all bins in the sample. An event is a run of flagged bins of the same sign, with at most one unflagged bin between two flagged ones. Its window is [t0, t1): t0 is the open of the first flagged bin and t1 the close of the last, UTC clock times, the same for every MM in the event.
  • Active MM: a labelled HYPE MM with at least one post-only (ALO) fill in the 2 hours before the event and at least one fill inside it.
  • sig24: the MM's own position scale, in HYPE, recomputed for each event from its positions over the 24 hours before t0. It is the largest of three numbers: 1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the position from its trailing 6-hour median, 2% of its 95th-percentile absolute position, and $12,500 of HYPE at the t0 mid.
  • Shocked: the MM's HYPE position changed from t0 to t1 by at least 3 sig24 (at least $37,500). It is decided per MM per event: the same MM can be shocked in one event and unshocked in the next.
  • End rule, peak rule: the end rule flags |position at t1 − position at t0| ≥ 3 sig24; the peak rule applies the same test to the largest gap from the t0 position at any minute inside the window.
  • Absorption side, exit side: the absorption side is the maker side the event's takers trade against (the bid when takers sell, the ask when takers buy); an MM filled there builds a position against the flow. The exit (opposite) side is the other one.
  • Absorber, absorption share: an absorber is an active MM with maker fills on the absorption side during the event. Absorption rank orders them by that maker USD, 1 = largest.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • Wfocus: the shortest interval inside the analysis window that holds 80% of the trough-to-peak mid move.
  • Surge onset (replays): the first second at which the 30-second sum of hit-side taker USD reaches 3 times the 95th percentile of that sum over the previous 6 hours.
  • Peer median: the median over every other MM holding a resting quote in the same window.
  • F1, F2, F3: F1: the 922 one-sided side surges. F2: the 399 half hours in which both sides surge. F3: the 327 F1 events the net-flow rule never selects.
  • Recall, lift: recall is the share of the 181 roster shocks that fall inside a rule's events; lift is how many times more often a flagged bin holds a roster shock than a random bin.
  • Event classes: liquidation cascade: forced flow at least 10% of taker USD; otherwise big price move: the mid moved at least 168 bps from start to end, the top 5% of all half hours; otherwise no big price move.
  • One-sided, two-sided: an event is one-sided when the hit side's taker USD surges and the other side's does not; two-sided when both surge.
  • Effective N, C, D: effective N is 1 over the sum of squared absorption shares: the number of equal absorbers that would be as concentrated. C is the largest MM's share of summed absolute inventory change. D is net over gross inventory change: 1 when every MM moved the same way.
  • A, L, t*: A is the most HYPE the MM built on the absorption side inside the window, counted from its position at t0; t* is the first minute attaining it. L is how far the position at t* sits from the MM's median position over the 6 hours before t0. Both are compared with the same sig24.
  1. Which market trigger the paper carries. Recommended: 30-minute bins, |zNET| in its top 5% (915 events) as the working catalogue, with the bins at 6 or more on the same scale (300 events) as the strict subset. The price-first trigger of §3.4 is a different object and finds roster shocks with a quarter of the lift; report it as the literature's definition applied to HYPE, not as the shock definition.
  2. In-sample or trailing cutoff. The trailing 30-day quantile costs 1.7 points of recall and drops 96 of the 915 events and adds 99 (921 in all). A referee will ask, and switching now is cheap.
  3. The price gate of record. The report uses the absolute gate (|move| at or above 168 bps, the overall 30-minute p95) and keeps the relative flag (the move against its own trailing week) as a column. Confirm p95 against p90 (129 bps, 54% of events big) or p99 (271 bps, 15%).
  4. Whether the imbalance ratio stays in the paper. It is not a shock detector for HYPE. One paragraph as a documented negative result may still be worth it, since the meeting asked for it by name.
  5. The standing surge-onset rule and W_focus rule for replays: 3 times the trailing 6-hour p95 of the 30-second hit-side taker sum, and the shortest interval holding 80% of the trough-to-peak tick move. Both were fixed before the second replay so the two are comparable; confirm or change before a third.
  6. Idiosyncratic against systemic on the market trigger. The proposed C≥0.6 threshold is unreachable (maximum 0.599); the label should live on the wallet trigger (Exp8's ALONE class) or the market-side rule should be restated on D alone.
  7. The price extreme window for the early and late split. §4.4 reads the price extreme over the event window plus 30 minutes, because the extreme of 22% of events falls on the last minute of the window. Measuring it inside the window alone moves 3,290 MM-event rows from late-held to late-peak and keeps the same label for 91.1% of rows. Confirm the 30-minute extension.
  8. Which shock scale is the one of record on the population: the position scale used here (spread of the position around its trailing median, with floors) or the spread of 30-minute position changes, which is zero for 37% of wallet-events.
  9. Control matching. Controls are matched on clock time and length; whether to add a volume or volatility match (nearest half hour by total taker USD) before the peer-response result is quoted.
  10. Whether the start-level peak rule is carried beside the end rule (§8.5). It flags 43.7% of top-5 absorber rows against 23.9% for the end rule. It adds 17 points to absorption ranks 6 to 20 and 1.5 points to the other active MMs. It cuts the events with none of the top five flagged from 351 to 134 of 914, every date included. Carrying it as a second flag makes the shocked population 65% larger and requires rerunning §4 and everything downstream of the flag. The pre-2h median baseline is not a candidate: it mixes pre-window drift into the event.
  11. Whether the two-sided family's 1-minute extent is measured on excess total taker USD (above its usual level) (§9.5), the construction used, or on raw total taker USD, which puts half of every window inside the run. This has to be settled before the MM results are computed on F2.

17.2 Labels and framing

Terms used here: Forced, voluntary flow, Roster, form_start, peak, Episode, Peer median
  • Forced, voluntary flow: forced flow is taker USD from liquidations and auto-deleveraging (ADL); voluntary flow is all other taker USD. A victim is the wallet that was force-closed.
  • Roster: the ten named HYPE MMs, MM01 to MM10, of the earlier per-wallet shock study.
  • form_start, peak: the peak is the 5-minute bin with the largest inventory deviation; form_start is the start of the shortest interval ending at the peak that holds 80% of the run-up.
  • Episode: a group of roster shocks that overlap in time.
  • Peer median: the median over every other MM holding a resting quote in the same window.
  1. MM types. Option A (carriers, which hold a shock for hours, against flatteners, which are back within minutes, on the half-life alone, transferable to the population), B (adds flatteners that unwind with taker orders against those that unwind with maker orders), or C (adds multi-coin against HYPE-only carriers; best separation, but MM05 sits alone). The population scatter (§5.3) shows the position scale tracks book size, which argues for typing on book size directly.
  2. "Shock" against "extreme event".
    The meeting's cutoffs are two orders of magnitude looser than the published extreme-event standard (99.9th percentile); §3.4 shows the two definitions select different events. The two objects need different names in the paper.
  3. A fifth absorption story.
    MM05 and MM08 were neither slow nor run through; they kept re-posting near-best quotes, with two orders of magnitude more size than peers, while the takers kept hitting them. Whether to add "re-armed" beside Exp10's closer, did-not-pull, run-through and size, and to measure it across the catalogue.
  4. Quote withdrawal as its own event type.
    MM05 posted no ask order for 209 seconds in the middle of the move with 213,000 HYPE of standing asks a minute earlier; this is invisible at 5-minute grain.
  5. One shock or three
    for 2026-01-20. The price moved 533 bps with three waves of liquidations. The Exp8 catalogue calls it one episode with three roster shocks, all peaking at 17:45. The largest single liquidation cluster of the window (16:45, $2.54m in one millisecond) sits outside every formation window (form_start to peak).

17.3 Follow-ups

Terms used here: HYPE MM, Control window, Forced, voluntary flow, Wallet codes, Event classes
  • HYPE MM: a wallet the project's daily label model (v5d) classes as a HYPE market maker on that date. The label is per date.
  • Control window: for each event, the same UTC clock time and length on the nearest date (+1, −1, +2, −2, … days) with no event in the window or within 2 hours of it. Controls are not matched on volume or volatility.
  • Forced, voluntary flow: forced flow is taker USD from liquidations and auto-deleveraging (ADL); voluntary flow is all other taker USD. A victim is the wallet that was force-closed.
  • Wallet codes: T01 to T10 are the largest takers of a replay, X## the largest non-roster makers, V01 the largest liquidated wallet. Codes are local to a section: the same code can name another wallet elsewhere.
  • Event classes: liquidation cascade: forced flow at least 10% of taker USD; otherwise big price move: the mid moved at least 168 bps from start to end, the top 5% of all half hours; otherwise no big price move.
  1. Re-run Exp9 and Exp10 with the 5-minute bin offset and report whether the headline quoting responses move.
  2. Re-anchor the dense panel's inventory level at source
    , or document the daily re-anchor as the required read pattern.
  3. Run the tick-level replay on 2025-08-14
    (−1,192 bps, 38% of taker USD from liquidations) as the bigger liquidation illustration, if the cross-margin question can be dropped there for want of account state.
  4. Test whether leaning into forced flow is a trait of X05 and X06.
    These are the codes of the 2026-01-20 liquidation replay, not the X05 and X06 of the two August episodes. Two HYPE MMs put half their maker dollars on liquidation legs in the 2026-01-20 window. Whether that is stable across events is Olga's predation-versus-absorption question in its cleanest form.
  5. Joint distribution of |return| and forced share
    over all 132k 15-minute windows, to say whether big price moves and liquidation cascades occur nearly independently.
  6. Measure the MM results on the three side-surge families
    (§9.5). F1 is done (§9.7) and the population pipeline now accepts an event list for a family; F2 and F3 need about 4 hours of compute each with the order stream. The open sub-decision is whether the matched controls for a family exclude only that family's events or the 915 as well.

Appendix: data sources

Every result covers the HYPE perpetual on Hyperliquid from 2025-03-27 to 2026-06-30 UTC, unless its section names a narrower window.

  • Taker fills. Every HYPE taker fill, grouped by taker order with its level-by-level fills aggregated (grouped_trade_oid). Whole-market taker flow per 5-minute and 30-minute bin is built from these fills.
  • Taker-maker pairs. Each taker order's fills paired with the maker orders they filled against (trade_pairs).
  • Order store. The raw HYPE limit-order store: every placement, cancel and fill with its status rows (orders_hype and the 2026 store).
  • Tick book. The HYPE order book strictly before and after the events at each timestamp (ts_bookdiff_lt and ts_bookdiff_le).
  • Mid prices. Canonical 5-minute mids for ten coins, including BTC, ETH and SOL, used for the cross-coin checks.
  • Account snapshots. Account-state snapshots across all coins, 2 to 5.5 hours apart, from 2025-09-27: equity, positions, liquidation prices and margin mode.
  • Fills with margin state and liquidations.
    Execution-ordered fills for ten coins with the account's margin state, and the liquidation trade records.
  • MM labels. The v5d label model's per-date HYPE market-maker labels.
  • Dense MM panel. A 5-minute panel of HYPE MM fills and orders (hype_mm_5m), used for the closed-PnL baseline and for fill and submit counts. Its carried inventory level is not used (§15).
  • Exp8 roster catalogue. Exp8's frozen catalogue of 181 inventory shocks on the roster ten.

Wallets appear by code. No wallet address appears in any table or figure.
